classification.difficultyReason: Identify three adjacent angles using square-grid geometry and inverse tangent, then explain their right-angle sum.

content.prompt: Explain how the diagram below shows that $\tan^{-1}(1)+\tan^{-1}\left(\frac12\right)+\tan^{-1}\left(\frac13\right)=90^\circ$.

spec.description: Two-column, three-row square grid with three joined vertices and three coloured sectors filling the bottom-left right angle. Free-form TikZ is required because the blank-grid template does not express the segments and angle sectors.
spec.mathematics: With bottom-left origin O, the other vertices are P=(1,3) and Q=(2,2). The three adjacent angles are atan(1), atan(1/2), and atan(1/3).
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied grid, segments and coloured sectors are visible; no angle values or added vertex labels are supplied.

answer.short: The red, blue and orange angles are respectively $\tan^{-1}(1)$, $\tan^{-1}(\frac12)$ and $\tan^{-1}(\frac13)$. They fill a right angle, so their sum is $90^\circ$.
answer.worked:
Let $O$ be the bottom-left corner, $P$ the upper vertex and $Q$ the right-hand vertex. Take each grid cell to have side length $1$.

For the red angle $\alpha$, the rise and run are both $2$:
$$\begin{align*}\tan\alpha&=\frac22=1\\\alpha&=\tan^{-1}(1).\end{align*}$$
For the orange angle $\gamma$, measured from the vertical, the opposite side is $1$ and the adjacent side is $3$:
$$\begin{align*}\tan\gamma&=\frac13\\\gamma&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac13\right).\end{align*}$$
The segments $OQ$ and $PQ$ are perpendicular: they follow diagonals of squares with opposite slopes. Also, $OQ=2\sqrt2$ and $PQ=\sqrt2$. Thus, for the blue angle $\beta$ in right-angled triangle $OPQ$,
$$\begin{align*}\tan\beta&=\frac{PQ}{OQ}\\\tan\beta&=\frac{\sqrt2}{2\sqrt2}=\frac12\\\beta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac12\right).\end{align*}$$
The three coloured angles fill the right angle at $O$. Therefore,
$$\tan^{-1}(1)+\tan^{-1}\left(\frac12\right)+\tan^{-1}\left(\frac13\right)=90^\circ.$$
